In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Quasi Newton approximation is the most efficient way of approximating the derivatives in 2D LCL.
Broyden's method is superior to 1D derivatives when the number of iterations is low.
the Broyden's method with 1D derivatives gives a good tradeoff between accuracy and computation times.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Quasi Newton method is the best method for 2D LCl inversion.
1D derivatives should not be used for the full 2d solution, but can be used in combination with Quasi Newton for an efficient 2D Lci solution.
1D derivatives are not sufficient for 2D LCL, Broyden’s formula is not sufficient either, but a combination of both gives very promising results and is the most time efficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to use 1D approximations in the inversion of continuous resistivity profiles without compromising the quality of the solution.
the combination of Broyden update formula and 2D Lateral constrained inversion (2DLCI) gives a fast and accurate solution to the 2D LTI inversion.
2D LCL can be run in a time frame that makes it a viable interpretation option for marine CSEM.
